annualCarTax.title: Annual Car Tax Calculator
annualCarTax.subtitle: Enter engine size and first registration date to get your {year} Korean annual car tax, the June/December installments, and the January lump-sum discount.

window.next: Days until the {m}/{y} lump-sum window opens. Pay the full year between {m}/16 and {dm}/{dd} to save {saved} KRW (about {pct}%) on this car.
window.open: The {m}/{y} lump-sum window is open now (closes {dm}/{dd}). Apply and pay within the window to save {saved} KRW (about {pct}%) on this car.
window.shifted: The month-end falls on a weekend, so the deadline moves to the next weekday (Framework Act on Local Taxes, Art. 24).

kindHint.car: Gasoline, diesel, LPG and hybrid cars. Taxed per cc, with age reductions from year 3 for non-commercial cars (none for commercial).
kindHint.ev: Electric, hydrogen and solar passenger cars pay a flat rate regardless of size. No age reduction.
kindHint.van: 11-15 seat vans are taxed at the small general bus flat rate.
kindHint.truck: Flat rate by payload. 1-ton trucks fall under 'up to 1 ton'.

use.label: Use
use.hint: Commercial means licensed transport businesses such as taxis and rental cars. Company cars are usually non-commercial.

u.ccHint: Enter the displacement (cc) shown on your registration certificate.
u.regHint: Based on the first registration date, not the model year. Cars registered in Jul-Dec have different ages for the June and December installments.
u.tonHint: Trucks over 10 tons pay extra per 10 tons; check with your local tax office.
u.yearNote: {y} is an estimate assuming current rates and the 5% lump-sum rate stay the same.

share.label: My {year} car tax (annual)
share.text: My {year} car tax is {total} KRW a year. Paying in January saves {saved} KRW.

lump.title: How much a lump-sum payment saves
lump.desc: Paying the whole year in advance deducts {rate}% annual interest on the tax for the remaining period. The earlier, the more you save.
lump.note: Deduction (Local Tax Act Art. 128(3)): January/March = annual tax × days from the day after the deadline to Dec 31 ÷ 365 × 5%; June = 2nd-half tax × 5%; September = 2nd-half tax × remaining days ÷ 184 × 5%. Education tax shrinks with it. May differ from your bill by tens of won.

prorate.title: Selling or scrapping mid-year (pro rata)
prorate.desc: If ownership changes or the car is deregistered during the year, tax is charged only for the days owned. Enter the transfer or deregistration date to see each share.
prorate.before: Jan 1 to day before ({days} days) · seller
prorate.after: That day to Dec 31 ({days} days) · buyer
prorate.refund: If you paid in January, about {amount} KRW refundable
prorate.note: Enforcement Decree Art. 126: annual tax × days owned ÷ days in year. The refund is an estimate reflecting the discount you received.

series.title: Tax by vehicle age
series.desc: How the annual tax (incl. education tax) on the same {cc}cc car falls as it ages. Assumes Jan-Jun registration.
series.note: 5% per year from year 3, capped at 50% from year 12 (Local Tax Act Art. 127(1)(2), non-commercial passenger cars).

u.disclaimer: Estimate based on the Local Tax Act. Exemptions for disabled persons, veterans, etc., trucks over 10 tons, special vehicles and express/charter buses are not included. Check your Wetax bill for the exact amount.

lump.title: How to pay in a lump sum
items: Apply and pay between the 16th and month-end in January, March, June or September. Applying without paying gets no discount.
Use Wetax (wetax.go.kr) or the Smart Wetax app; Seoul residents can use ETAX. District tax offices also accept it.
Auto-debit for regular installments does not cover lump-sum payment.
After one January lump-sum payment, a January bill may be sent in following years. The 2026 rate is 5%, same as 2024-2025.

age.title: Vehicle age reduction
items: Age counts from the first registration date, not the model year.
Registered Jan-Jun: tax year − registration year + 1.
Registered Jul-Dec: June installment uses the year difference, December adds 1.
5% from year 3, +5% each year, up to 50% from year 12. Applies only to cc-based non-commercial passenger cars (not commercial, EV, van or truck).

refund.title: Selling, scrapping, moving
items: After a lump-sum payment, selling or deregistering refunds the unowned days pro rata.
When you buy a used car, you owe the share from the transfer date to year-end.
Moving to another district after paying does not trigger a new charge that year.
Regular bills go to the owner as of June 1 and December 1, split by ownership period.

tips.title: Good to know
items: Car tax is an annual property-type tax. The one-time acquisition tax on purchase is calculated in the car acquisition tax calculator.
Compact cars get no car tax exemption; they simply pay 80 KRW/cc. Their perks are acquisition tax relief and fuel tax refunds.
Hybrids are taxed by engine displacement, not at the EV flat rate.
Late payment adds a 3% penalty plus monthly late-payment interest; unpaid tax can lead to plate seizure.

items.a: The rate is 5%, applied only to the remaining period (June and September cover the 2nd half only), so January saves about 4.58% of the annual tax, March ~3.77%, June ~2.5% and September ~1.25%. Education tax falls too.

items.q: How do I apply for lump-sum payment?
items.a: Between the 16th and month-end in January, March, June or September, look up your car on Wetax/Smart Wetax (ETAX in Seoul) and pay. Auto-debit does not apply.

items.q: Do I get a refund if I sell or scrap the car?
items.a: Yes. Tax for the period after the transfer or deregistration date is refunded pro rata (Enforcement Decree Art. 126). Moving districts does not trigger a new charge.
No car tax exemption. Up to 1,000cc is 80 KRW/cc, so a 998cc car pays about 100,000 KRW a year including education tax.

items.q: How much is car tax on an EV?
items.a: Non-commercial EVs and hydrogen cars pay 100,000 KRW plus 30,000 KRW education tax = 130,000 KRW. Commercial: 20,000 KRW. No age reduction.

From the first registration date. Jan-Jun registrations: tax year − registration year + 1. Jul-Dec: June uses the difference, December adds 1. Non-commercial passenger cars get 5% off from year 3, up to 50% from year 12.

items.q: Are company cars taxed as commercial?
items.a: No. Commercial means licensed transport businesses such as taxis, rental cars and freight carriers. Company passenger cars usually pay non-commercial rates.

items.q: How is this different from acquisition tax?
items.a: Acquisition tax is paid once when you buy a car; car tax is paid every June and December while you own it.
